title: Many-sorted relational logic: domains and guarded quantifiers
summary: Give variables separate domains and translate relational formulas into ordinary first-order logic using sort predicates and guarded quantifiers.
abstract: Membership connects an element with a set, so its two arguments play different roles. Many-sorted logic records such distinctions by giving variables different domains. We show how to express those domains inside ordinary first-order logic: a predicate marks each sort, and a quantifier is restricted by a guard. The translation preserves truth, and its ordinary models recover genuine sorted models once every sort is required to be nonempty. Working through both directions explains why adding sorts preserves compactness and why the guards for universal and existential quantifiers have different forms.
